_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war LIVE — Section 338 50% tariffs operative since Aug 22; Canada 700+ line C$27.6B retaliation effective Sept 8 (5 days); no diplomatic off-ramp; Trump 50% auto tariff threat Jan 1 2027
themes.summary: As of September 3, the Canada-US trade war remains at maximum escalation with Canada's September 8 retaliatory tariff effective date now five days away and no diplomatic channel open. The US Section 338 50% tariffs on C$27.6 billion of Canadian goods have been operative since August 22 — covering dairy, alcohol, building materials, electronics, apparel, and agricultural goods — and apply even to CUSMA-compliant goods with no statutory expiry. Canada's Department of Finance published the complete counter-tariff list on August 25, confirming C$27.6 billion in US imports across 700+ tariff lines at rates of 15%, 25%, and 50% matched to US Section 338 and Section 232 rates, effective 12:01 a.m. September 8. Sectors targeted include steel and aluminum (duties doubled to 50%), dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, plastics, and electronics. One notable nuance: Canada quietly removed its older pre-existing retaliatory tariffs on CUSMA-compliant US goods effective September 1 — a gesture of de-escalation on legacy duties — but this is categorically separate from the new September 8 counter-tariff list responding to Section 338, which is fully intact and unaffected. Finance Minister Champagne also announced a multi-billion-dollar business support package alongside the counter-tariff list. Trade negotiations collapsed on the night of August 21-22, with USTR Greer saying Canada 'wanted more' than Washington was willing to offer in the final hours, while PM Carney said the US proposed terms that were 'neither fair nor economically sound.' No evidence of diplomatic reopening has emerged since. The September 8 binary is the immediate live tripwire: the question is whether Washington responds to Canada's retaliation with a counter-escalation or absorbs it. Trump's separate threat to impose 50% tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel effective January 1, 2027 adds a structural medium-term CAD negative beyond the immediate Sept 8 catalyst. USDCAD has been trading in the 1.39 area, supported by the dual tailwind of structural CAD weakness from the tariff shock and USD strength from the Warsh hawkish repricing. Canada's smaller trade-oriented economy is widely acknowledged as more vulnerable to the escalation than that of the US.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM CAD negative — US 50% tariffs live since Aug 22, full 700+ line retaliation list published with Sept 8 effective date (5 days), negotiations explicitly collapsed, Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat adds structural overhang. USDCAD ~1.39, approaching/probing key 1.3900. BoC rate hike expectations further compressed as tariff growth drag dominates. Sept 8 is the next hard catalyst: US counter-retaliation = USDCAD accelerates above 1.40; US silence/absorption = modest near-term CAD relief but structural weakness remains. Canada's de-escalation gesture on legacy CUSMA duties (Sept 1) provides a thin diplomatic fig leaf but has not reopened talks.
implications.USD: USDCAD directionally bullish from tariff shock, reinforced by post-Warsh hawkish USD repricing (CME FedWatch 65-68% Sep hike). Canada tariff shock adds modest USD safe-haven bid vs commodity bloc.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture keeps uncertainty elevated. Congress.gov CRS notes divergence in US-Mexico vs US-Canada bilateral negotiating progress adds uncertainty premium.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on CAD weakness. Broader protectionism signal from Section 338 invocation has limited but non-zero EUR contagion.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc contagion — AUD trades defensively in acute CAD-shock episodes. AUDUSD subject to additional headwind from post-Warsh USD strength; vulnerable to further risk-off from US-Canada escalation spiral post Sept 8.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path and post-Warsh USD dynamics.
implications.JPY: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus structural JPY bid from BOJ Sep hike cycle.

themes.watchLevel: USDCAD 1.3900 is the immediate live test — a clean daily close above 1.3900 opens 1.4017-1.4021 (50-day EMA area) and then 1.4100. Post-Warsh USD tailwind (65-68% Sep hike odds on CME) makes 1.40 a plausible near-term target absent a diplomatic surprise. USDCAD 1.3800-1.3820 is near-term downside support; a close below 1.3780 would require a surprise diplomatic reopening. Sept 8 Canada retaliation effective date: US counter-retaliation = USDCAD accelerates above 1.40; US silence/absorption = modest near-term CAD relief rally toward 1.3850. Canada's Sept 1 removal of legacy CUSMA-compliant duties is the only de-escalation signal so far — insufficient to change the structural direction. Jan 1 2027 automotive tariff threat (50% on all Canadian cars, trucks, parts) is a structural medium-term CAD negative even if Sept 8 passes without escalation. Theme ends only on: (1) formal re-opening of US-Canada talks with credible framework, or (2) Trump executive action suspending Section 338.

themes.title: BOJ Sep 17-18 hike ~73% priced — Ueda (Sep 1 G20) signals live debate, Takata (Sep 2 Sapporo) calls for nimble hikes; 2yr JGB at 1.83% (30-yr high); USDJPY grinding 160.33 RSI 70; intervention regime at 160
themes.summary: As of September 3, the BOJ September 17-18 rate hike narrative has materially strengthened since the last update, with two major communication events in the past 48 hours cementing the case. First, BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda on September 1 at the G20 finance leaders' gathering in Asheville, North Carolina, signalled a strong chance of a September hike, saying the BOJ would set policy 'mindful of upside risks to inflation' and that the board would 'debate these factors thoroughly, including at our next policy meeting.' Ueda appeared alongside Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama, and confirmed a bilateral meeting with US Treasury Secretary Bessent, who has publicly called for 'decisive' monetary steps to combat the weak yen — cementing the US-Japan policy coordination signal. Second, hawkish board member Hajime Takata, speaking in Sapporo on September 2, said 2026 marks a 'significant turning point' requiring the BOJ to respond 'more flexibly' rather than remain 'bound by a set pace or magnitude of rate hikes' — an explicit call for acceleration beyond the roughly twice-yearly pace. Takata, who was the sole dissenter at the July meeting in favour of an immediate hike to 1.25%, declined to pre-commit on timing but said decisions should be made 'on a meeting-by-meeting basis.' The combined effect of Ueda and Takata communications has lifted the 2-year JGB yield to 1.83%, its highest level since 1995, and driven market pricing to approximately 73% for a September hike. USDJPY traded at 160.33 on September 2 with RSI at 70, grinding the upper edge of the intervention regime threshold. The US-Japan joint intervention regime established in late July — which spent approximately $58.97 billion driving USDJPY to 155.27 — remains structurally intact with the 160.00 level as the live line. Reuters sources have confirmed the BOJ is set to raise rates as soon as September and is considering hiking more aggressively thereafter than the current pace of roughly twice a year. BOJ current rate is 1.00% (June hike); a September hike would take it to 1.25%. The next calendar event is the Masu speech on September 10, followed by the hard binary of the BOJ September 17-18 meeting.

implications.JPY: Three-pillar structural JPY support in cross-current with post-Warsh USD strength: (1) Intervention regime — 160.00 being tested in real time with USDJPY at 160.33 on Sep 2, RSI 70, MoF/BOJ credibility on the line; (2) BOJ Sep hike ~73% priced, Ueda (Sep 1 G20) and Takata (Sep 2 Sapporo) both delivered hawkish communications, 2yr JGB at 1.83% 30-year high, Reuters/MUFG confirm Sep + Jan 2027 double-hike trajectory; (3) Bessent-Ueda bilateral at G20 Asheville cements US-Japan policy coordination signal. Net: intervention threat and Sep 17-18 BOJ hike binary are acute and imminent; post-Warsh USD strength adds near-term upside pressure but medium-term direction is JPY-bullish.
implications.USD: USDJPY topside meets intervention threat at 160.00 — the level is being tested at 160.33. Post-Warsh hawkish repricing (65-68% Sep hike, 10yr UST at 4.79%) is the dominant near-term USD support. Rate differential direction of travel is USD-negative vs JPY from both sides over medium term.
implications.EUR: EURJPY under pressure from intervention mechanism and BOJ hike pricing. 2yr JGB at 1.83% 30-year high narrows EUR-JPY rate differential.
implications.GBP: GBPJPY under dual intervention and carry-unwind pressure. GBPUSD subject to post-Warsh USD strength.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY lower on intervention pressure. SNB in easing mode.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ hike cycle.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention pressure. AUDUSD reversed multi-month highs on post-Warsh USD strength.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention pressure; NZDUSD retraced from recent highs on post-Warsh USD strength.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY 160.00 is the LIVE critical line — at 160.33 on Sep 2 with RSI 70, the intervention regime is under acute stress. A daily close above 160.50 without MoF verbal or actual intervention signals carry traders have overpowered the regime and a test of 162-163 becomes possible. Masu speech Sep 10 is the final pre-meeting BOJ communication and the last chance to validate or push back on Sep hike expectations. BOJ Sep 17-18 is the hard binary: hike to 1.25% = USDJPY likely drops toward 155-152, 2yr JGB yield pulls back from 1.83% high; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 160+ re-test, intervention regime faces acute stress. USDJPY below 158.00 = intervention credibility reasserting. USDJPY below 155.27 (post-intervention low) = regime decisively winning. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately. Ueda declining to commit at Sep 17-18 (hawkish hold) = partial unwind of 73% pricing but theme remains active.

themes.title: Warsh hawkish repricing — Sep hike odds 65-68% on CME FedWatch; 10yr UST at 4.79% (Jan 2025 high); Barclays calls Sep+Dec double hike; NEXT: Sep 4 payrolls (TODAY), Sep 11 CPI, Sep 16 FOMC
themes.summary: As of September 3, the Warsh hawkish repricing from Jackson Hole remains fully intact with CME FedWatch showing 65-68% probability of a September 16 hike — more than double the roughly 36% priced before Warsh's August 28 keynote. The 10-year Treasury yield has risen to approximately 4.79%, its highest level since January 2025, reflecting the durable repricing of the rate path. The Warsh Jackson Hole keynote flagged PCE at 3.7% over 12 months and 4.1% over six months — both 'well above the 2% target' — and described underlying inflation as 'not slowing,' while arguing financial conditions are not genuinely restrictive. Bank of America economist Aditya Bhave concluded that 'absent a material downside surprise, the onus is now on Warsh to deliver a September hike.' Barclays has upgraded its call to two 2026 hikes — September and December — totaling 50 basis points. Governor Lisa Cook has separately noted headline and core inflation are running about 1 percentage point above expectations, driven by core goods prices rising at a 5% annual pace. The backdrop: the July FOMC vote was 9-3 to hold (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan dissented for a hike, the most dissents since September 2016), and the June dot plot showed nine members projecting at least one 2026 hike. Steve Hanke sees the hike probability closer to 80%, noting Warsh could join the three dissenters and influence additional members. As of September 2, JOLTS July job openings data and August ISM Manufacturing PMI have been released — results were being digested. September 4 nonfarm payrolls (today) are the next critical real-time growth check, followed by September 11 August CPI as the definitive pre-FOMC inflation tiebreaker. Goldman Sachs (Hatzius) continues to forecast core CPI and PCE around 0.2% MoM in August, consistent with a hold, illustrating that the Sep 11 print is genuinely pivotal. Chicago PMI missed at 47.1 vs 57.9 expected on August 28, adding a growth caution counterpoint — the stagflation narrative (hot inflation, softening activity) is the key risk to how far hike pricing can extend.

implications.USD: DXY holding post-Warsh hawkish gains, 10yr UST at 4.79% (Jan 2025 high). CME FedWatch at 65-68% Sep hike. Sep 4 payrolls (today): strong (200k+, unemployment flat) = cements 70%+ hike odds, DXY targets 100.50-101.00; weak (below 150k, unemployment rising) = stagflation narrative limits hike pricing, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 11 August CPI is the critical pre-FOMC tiebreaker: hot (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = Sep hike above 75%, DXY toward 100.50-101.00, EURUSD toward 1.1350-1.1450; soft (core at or below 0.2% MoM per Goldman base) = hike odds pull back toward 50%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy binary.
implications.JPY: Warsh hawkish outcome partially restores rate differential, creating cross-current against BOJ Sep hike narrative. USDJPY at 160.33 Sep 2 — intervention regime tested. Net: post-Warsh USD support is a USDJPY upside force, BOJ Sep hike (~73% priced) + intervention regime is a USDJPY downside force. Sep 4 payrolls and Sep 11 CPI move both sides of the USDJPY equation simultaneously.
implications.EUR: EURUSD has retraced from 1.1657 toward 1.1500-1.1550 on Warsh hawkish repricing. Sep 11 US CPI and Sep 16 FOMC are the next major EURUSD catalysts. ECB dynamics provide partial offset.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD subject to post-Warsh USD strength. Rate convergence story has partially shifted back in USD's favour. BoE's own path and UK data remain independent GBP drivers.
implications.CAD: Post-Warsh USD strength adds a second tailwind to USDCAD alongside the Section 338 tariff shock. USDCAD probing 1.39. Stagflation narrative (Chicago PMI 47.1 miss) limits how far rate hike pricing can extend if Sep 4 payrolls disappoint.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD partially reversed multi-month highs on Warsh hawkish USD repricing. Sep 4 payrolls are a dual AUD catalyst: strong = USD bid keeps AUDUSD capped; weak = risk-off plus stagflation narrative weighs on AUD independently.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDUSD retraced from recent highs on Warsh USD bid.
implications.CHF: USDCHF lifted by Warsh hawkish repricing. SNB easing mode limits CHF upside. CHF safe-haven bid provides partial offset in risk-off episodes.

themes.watchLevel: Sep 4 payrolls (TODAY — the highest-impact near-term event): strong (200k+, unemployment unchanged or lower) = cements 70%+ hike odds, DXY toward 100.50; weak (below 150k or unemployment rising) = stagflation narrative caps hike pricing, DXY loses post-Warsh gains toward 98.50. Sep 11 August CPI is the critical pre-FOMC tiebreaker: hot (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = Sep hike above 75%, DXY toward 100.50-101.00, EURUSD toward 1.1350-1.1450; soft (core at or below 0.2% MoM per Goldman base case) = hike odds pull back toward 50%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy binary: hike 25bps to 3.75-4.00% = full hawkish validation, DXY toward 101-102, EURUSD below 1.1300; hold with hawkish dots (2026 median above 4.00%) = partial validation; hold with unchanged dots = sell-the-news USD weakness. DXY closing and sustaining below 98.00 = Warsh hawkish read fully unwound. 10yr UST at 4.79% is a key watch level — a sustained move above 4.85% would signal full Sep hike pricing plus a Dec hike beginning to be discounted (consistent with Barclays double-hike call).
